title: Query performance measurement harness (foundational)
description: A harness runs a representative query workload against the current index and records latency and recall per query. The workload is sampled from real retrieval history so measurements reflect actual use, not synthetic benchmarks. Every measurement is timestamped and stored for trend analysis. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
import time
workload = ['index latency', 'posting lists', 'hash verify']
for q in workload:
    t0 = time.perf_counter(); time.sleep(0.001); dt = time.perf_counter() - t0
    print(f'{q}: {dt*1000:.2f}ms')
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Self-Improving Index Builder practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Index variant A/B testing (foundational)
description: Candidate index structures are built side by side and tested on the same workload, with each variant measured independently. The comparison uses paired statistics so query-to-query variance does not masquerade as a structural difference. Only a variant that wins significantly replaces the incumbent. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Self-Improving Index Builder practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Structure selection by workload fit (foundational)
description: The builder selects index structures by workload characteristics: point lookups favor hash indexes, range scans favor trees, text search favors inverted indexes. Selection rules are explicit and reviewable, not learned black boxes. Mixed workloads get composite structures with a routing layer. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Self-Improving Index Builder practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Incremental index rebuild (foundational)
description: When the structure changes, the index rebuilds incrementally: new writes go to the new structure while old segments migrate in the background. Incremental rebuild keeps the archive searchable throughout the transition. A cutover flag flips reads to the new structure only after verification passes. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
segments, migrated = 10, 0
while migrated < segments:
    migrated += 2  # background migration batches
print(f'migrated {migrated}/{segments} segments | reads still on old index until verified')
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Self-Improving Index Builder practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Improvement tracking dashboard data (foundational)
description: Every rebuild records before-and-after metrics: mean latency, p99 latency, recall, and index size. The tracking history proves whether the builder's changes actually helped over time. Regressions trigger automatic rollback to the previous structure. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
hist = [{'ver': 'v1', 'p99': 900}, {'ver': 'v2', 'p99': 320}]
print('p99 improvement:', hist[0]['p99'], '->', hist[1]['p99'], 'ms')
print('rollback' if hist[-1]['p99'] > hist[-2]['p99'] else 'keep v2')
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Self-Improving Index Builder practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.
